text: I learned storage management from my mother.
She survived a famine before I was born.
She never trusted full granaries.
She said abundance makes people careless.
I still think about the post–Night of Ash shortages.
Food disappeared faster than expected that year.
People argued about causes instead of rationing early.
I learned that delay is more dangerous than hunger.
Some villagers believe the temple demands too many offerings.
They are not always wrong.
Doran focuses on production.
I focus on loss.
Both matter, but only one is usually ignored.
I have found spoilage patterns that do not match weather reports.
Sometimes stored grain decays faster than expected.
I cannot explain why.
I began marking those storage batches separately.
I have not shared all of those records with Tarek.
He prefers optimistic reports.
Luma understands why I withhold certain details.
Nara believes food offerings affect spiritual balance.
I believe improper storage affects survival.
Both lead to different kinds of rituals.
Noki often listens more to Sena than to me.
That worries me.
The terraces are old, but stable.
Storage systems are newer, but fragile.
People underestimate how quickly systems fail.
I have prepared 'emergency reserves' in hidden locations.
Only Doran knows part of their existence.
